THIS MFA IS FILED U/S.173(1) OF MV ACT, PRAYING TO MODIFY THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD PASSED BY THE PRINCIPAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MACT-IV AT DAVANGERE IN MVC NO.450/2019 DATED 04.11.2019 AND TO ENHANCE THE COMPENSATION FROM RS.2,10,320/- TO RS.17,00,000/-
BY ALLOWING THIS APPEAL IN THE INTEREST OF EQUITY AND JUSTICE.
 THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THROUGH PHYSICAL HEARING/VIDEO CONFERENCING THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 04.11.2019 passed by the Principal Senior Civil Judge &
Member, MACT-IV, Davanagere (for short 'the Tribunal'), in MVC No.450/2019, the petitioner therein has preferred this appeal.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to herein as per their status before the Tribunal.
3. Brief facts of the case are as follows:

That on 22.02.2019 at about 12.30 p.m. the petitioner was a pillion rider in a motor bike bearing registration No.KA- 41/Y-5595 and when he reached KSRTC bus stand at P.B.Road, Davanagere, the rider of the motor bike drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to a road divider, because of which the petitioner fell down and got injured.
The offending motor bike is duly insured with the second respondent - Insurance Company.

Due to the accident, the petitioner sustained the following injuries:-
1. Lacerated wound over right forearm.
2. Fracture 1st MC right hand.
3. Fracture olecrenon right.
4.

The Tribunal, based on the evidence let in, has awarded a compensation of Rs.2,10,320/- along with interest @ 8% p.a. under the following heads:-
1 Pain and suffering Rs. 30,000/-
Food & nourishment, conveyance 2 Rs. 15,000/-
& attendant charges
Loss of income during laid up 3 Rs. 27,000/-

Not satisfied by the same, the petitioner has preferred this appeal.
6. The accident happened in the year 2019.
The petitioner was aged 60 years.
His income has not been established before the Tribunal.
Hence, the notional income as prescribed in the Lok-Adalath chart has to be considered which will be Rs.14,000/- per month.
According to the Tribunal, the petitioner has suffered permanent body disability at 12%, which in my opinion is correct.
The petitioner was aged 60 years at the time of accident.
Hence, the multiplier of '9' has to be adopted as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma & Ors vs Delhi Transport Corp.& Anr reported in 2009(6) SCC 121.

sentences.text:
Thus, towards 'loss of earning due to disability',
the petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.1,81,440/-(14,000x12x9x12%) as against Rs.90,720/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
With regard to 'loss of income during laid up period', the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.27,000/-.
Given the nature of injuries, the laid up period has to be considered atleast 3 months and a sum of Rs.42,000/- (14000x3=42,000/-) is awarded under this head.
Towards 'pain and suffering', the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.30,000/-.
Given the nature of injuries, I deem it appropriate to enhance it to Rs.40,000/-.

Towards 'food & nourishment,
conveyance & attendant charges', the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.15,000/-.

In my opinion,
the same is just and proper.
Towards 'medical expenses', based on the actual bills, a sum of Rs.37,600/- is awarded by the Tribunal.
I deem the same to be appropriate.
Towards 'loss of amenities and unhappiness', a sum of Rs.10,000/- is awarded by the Tribunal.
I deem it appropriate to enhance it to Rs.20,000/-.
7. Thus, the compensation to the petitioner under different heads is modified as hereunder:-
